newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan Shipping sees profits up.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan Shipping sees profits up.

text.p: The state-run Pakistan National Shipping Corporation (PNSC) said on Friday it expected its operating profit for financial 1996/97 (July-June) to be substantially higher than the previous year.
"PNSC has started on the path of profitability after several years of heavy losses," a PNSC statement said.
It said the PNSC moved back into the black in 1995/96, with an operating profit of 59 million rupees, compared to a loss of 528 million rupees in 1994/95.
Operating profit for the half-year ending December 31, 1996 was 103 million rupees. PNSC said it expected to achieve a similar figure in the second half of fiscal 1996/97.

It said the PNSC had last month repaid a third instalment of $6.734 million on a $50 million government-guaranteed loan obtained from the state-run National Bank of Pakistan in 1996 to finance the purchase of three German-made container vessels.
The acquisition of the three containers brought the national carrier's fleet to 17 vessels.

Each of the container ships has the potential to boost PNSC's earnings by an estimated $10,500 a day, the current market rate for chartering container services for ports in Far East, Singapore, Hong Kong, Korea and Taiwan, it said.
